 South Carolina State, North Carolina Central Set for Pivotal MEAC Showdown
 Football | 11/13/2026 3:45:46 PM
 Story Links
 Weekly Video Conference 
 Weekly Game Notes 
 NORFOLK, Va. – A highly anticipated matchup between South Carolina State and North Carolina Central headlines Week 11 action as the race for the MEAC championship enters its final stretch.
Delaware State travels to Howard in another matchup with championship implications, while Morgan State hosts Norfolk State.
 Week 11 Schedule 
Saturday, Nov. 14 
Norfolk State at Morgan State | 12:00 PM | ESPN+
Delaware State at Howard | 1:00 PM | ESPN+
North Carolina Central at South Carolina State | 1:30 PM | ESPN+
*All Times ET
 MEAC Football Notes 
 Bulldogs Host Eagles 
Both the Bulldogs and Eagles enter Saturday’s showdown riding three-game winning streaks. South Carolina State leads the nation in total defense, allowing just 250.2 yards per game, while North Carolina Central leads the country with 21 forced turnovers this season.
 MEAC in the Rankings 
South Carolina State, North Carolina Central and Delaware State represented the Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference (MEAC) in the latest Black College Football Poll.
South Carolina State rose to No. 1, while North Carolina Central and Delaware State came in at No. 7 and No. 8, respectively.

 Around the League 
 Bulldogs Keep Streaking 
 South Carolina State rallied for a 35-28 victory over Howard on Thursday night at Greene Stadium, scoring the game-winning touchdown with just 17 seconds remaining to secure its eighth win of the season. After the two teams traded scores throughout the contest, the Bulldogs put together a late scoring drive that was capped by Ricorian Brown’s 9-yard touchdown run.
 Brown had a standout night on the ground, finishing with 143 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries to lead the South Carolina State offense. Quarterback Keely Watson completed 21-of-29 passes for 241 yards and a touchdown as the Bulldogs totaled 384 yards of offense. The victory moved South Carolina State to 8-2 overall and 3-0 in MEAC play, keeping the Bulldogs unbeaten in conference action. Howard fell to 4-6 overall and 1-2 in the MEAC.
 Eagles’ Historic Comeback 
 North Carolina Central pulled off a dramatic 29-28 comeback victory over Norfolk State on Saturday at William “Dick” Price Stadium, scoring the go-ahead touchdown with 27 seconds remaining to complete the comeback. The Eagles trailed 21-7 at halftime but began to chip away in the third quarter, with Joshua Jones connecting with Luke Bracey on an 8-yard touchdown pass before Riley Daniels added a 25-yard field goal to make it a four-point game. Norfolk State extended its lead to 28-17 early in the fourth quarter on a 13-yard touchdown run by Jalyn Daniels, but North Carolina Central answered with a 7-yard touchdown run by Jones to pull within five.
 After Norfolk State missed a 25-yard field goal with 2:24 remaining, the Eagles took advantage of the opportunity. North Carolina Central recovered a fumble on the ensuing Norfolk State possession and moved 37 yards in five plays, with Jones finding Mehki Wall for a 26-yard touchdown pass with 27 seconds left. The Eagles attempted a two-point conversion to extend the lead, but the pass fell incomplete. Norfolk State had one final opportunity, moving into field goal range before missing a 37-yard attempt with four seconds remaining.
 Gino Addison led the North Carolina Central ground game with 174 yards on 18 carries, while Jones accounted for four touchdowns, throwing for 156 yards and three scores and adding a rushing touchdown. Tyree Saunders caught six passes for 60 yards and a touchdown, while Wall finished with four receptions for 38 yards and the late go-ahead score. Defensively, Khareem Thompson recorded six tackles, including three tackles for loss, a sack and a forced fumble. The victory improved North Carolina Central to 5-5 overall and 3-0 in MEAC play, while Norfolk State dropped to 4-6 and 0-3 in conference action.
 Hornets Stay in Contention 
 Delaware State earned a 24-14 victory over Morgan State on Saturday afternoon at Alumni Stadium, using a strong second-half performance. The Hornets took a 7-0 lead in the second quarter on a 2-yard touchdown run by Marqui Adams before Morgan State answered with a 1-yard scoring run by Cameron Edge to tie the game at halftime. Delaware State regained the lead in the third quarter when Adams connected with Kyree Benton for a 30-yard touchdown before Maatteo Bracalenti added a 25-yard field goal to make it 17-7.
 Morgan State cut the deficit to three early in the fourth quarter on Marquez Spells’ 60-yard punt return for a touchdown, but Phillip Dunnam sealed the victory for the Hornets with a 38-yard interception return for a touchdown with 2:09 remaining. Adams finished with 169 passing yards, a touchdown and 18 rushing yards, while Deontae Williams led the Hornets with 89 rushing yards. The victory moved Delaware State to 6-4 overall and 2-1 in MEAC play, while Morgan State fell to 5-5 overall and 0-3 in conference action.
 About the Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference 
The Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference (MEAC) enters its 56th year of intercollegiate competition with the 2026–27 academic year. Headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia, the MEAC is comprised of eight distinguished Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) along the Atlantic seaboard: Coppin State University, Delaware State University, Howard University, University of Maryland Eastern Shore, Morgan State University, Norfolk State University, North Carolina Central University, and South Carolina State University. Since its founding in 1970, the MEAC has been dedicated to promoting academic excellence, sportsmanship, and the personal growth of student athletes. For more information, visit www.MEACSports.com .
